keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox "c. 5500 - c. 4800 BCE"; the lead places the culture in "northern Mesopotamia"; sites Samarra, Tell es-Sawwan, Tell Shemshara, Yarim Tepe. Tell es-Sawwan, the type site, "lies on a 12 meter high cliff overlooking the Tigris River" (its page), where farmers "used irrigation from the" Tigris. Yarim Tepe (Sinjar) lies inside the Hassuna and Halaf shapes and is not drawn here. No area figure to compare.

ledger.note: 5500 BCE: the irrigation farmers of Samarra settle the middle Tigris. "roughly dated to between 5500 and 4800 BCE"; "evidence of irrigation-including flax-establishes the presence of a prosperous settled culture"; the Tell es-Sawwan ditch was "radiocarbon dated to 5730 +/- 75 B.C." (its page). The land south of the Hassuna piedmont had no culture on the map before.

ledger.note: 4800 BCE: the Samarra gives way to the Ubaid. "The Samarran Culture was the precursor to the Mesopotamian culture of the Ubaid period"; infobox "Followed by: Ubaid period"; the page does not say how it ended.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: two radii around excavated sites, never a frontier.

notes: Culture dossier. Choga Mami and the Mandali plain, usually counted as Samarran, are not on either page and are not drawn. The Samarra page names only Syria among modern countries (for Late Neolithic comparanda), not Iraq. Gazetteer: Tell es-Sawwan, Tell Shemshara are not places; radii around Samarra and As Sulaymaniyah stand in.
